title: Accommodation Approval via Unauthorized Channel During Investigation Hold
scenario_text:
**ServiceNow HR Case — CASE0013205**
Type: Workplace Investigation | Employee: Denise Okafor, Quality Engineer (Plant 3 — Mexico) | Opened: Oct 28, 2025
Status: On Hold (FMLA) | Hold Start: Nov 4, 2025 | Investigator: Craig Penner (separated Nov 22, 2025)
Case notes (Oct 28): 'Complaint filed by D. Okafor alleging hostile work environment. Named respondent: Shift Supervisor Ramos. Interim separation of duties implemented.'
Case notes (Nov 4): 'Okafor began FMLA leave (serious health condition). Investigation paused per ER SOP 7.3.'
Case notes (Nov 22): 'Penner's last day. Case reassignment pending.'
[No further case activity]

**ServiceNow HR Case — CASE0013288**
Type: Accommodation Request | Employee: Denise Okafor | Opened: Jan 8, 2026
Status: Open | Notes (Jan 8): 'Okafor returning from FMLA Jan 20. Requests modified schedule (no night shifts) citing ongoing treatment. Manager Ramos asked to provide essential functions analysis.'

**Microsoft Teams — DM between @luis.ramos and @karen.cho (Plant 3 HR Coordinator) (Jan 10, 2026, 3:22 PM)**
@luis.ramos: Karen can we just approve the no-nights thing? I don't want her on my shift anyway tbh. Less drama.
@karen.cho: I mean I can mark it approved in the system. She's a good worker when she's not causing problems.
@luis.ramos: Do it. I'll adjust the rotation.
@karen.cho: Done ✅

**ADP — Denise Okafor (Emp #5587)**
Classification: Salaried/Exempt | Location: Plant 3 (Monterrey) | FMLA Status: Approved through Jan 19, 2026 | Supervisor: Luis Ramos
Schedule Change Effective: Jan 20, 2026 — 'Day shift only per accommodation'

**SharePoint — /policies/hr/ada-interactive-process (v2.1, published Aug 2024)**
Section 3.2: 'All accommodation determinations require completion of the Interactive Process, including (a) identification of essential functions, (b) review by ER or designee with ADA training, and (c) documented good-faith dialogue with the employee. Direct supervisors may NOT approve accommodations unilaterally.'
Section 5.1: 'Where accommodation involves schedule modification, Workforce Planning must confirm operational feasibility before approval.'

**Outlook — From: craig.penner@ironforge.com To: natalie.brennan@ironforge.com (Nov 18, 2025)**
Subject: Okafor case — heads up before I go
> Nat — just flagging this one. Ramos is the named respondent in the harassment complaint. If Okafor comes back and needs anything routed through her manager, there's an obvious conflict. Make sure whoever picks this up knows not to loop Ramos into any decisions about her employment conditions. I left a note in the case but you know how things fall through the cracks here.

**Microsoft Teams — #hr-team (Jan 15, 2026, 9:05 AM)**
@karen.cho: Quick update — Okafor accommodation sorted. She's day shift starting the 20th.
@natalie.brennan: Wait, who ran the interactive process?
@karen.cho: Luis approved it, seemed straightforward.
[No further replies]
question: On Jan 15, 2026, Natalie discovers the accommodation was approved. What is the most critical compliance failure, and what must happen before Okafor's return on Jan 20?

contributor.name: Natalie Brennan
contributor.title: Employee Relations Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Workplace investigations, ADA interactive process, accommodation requests, conflict-of-interest protocols

choices: The accommodation was approved without Workforce Planning sign-off on operational feasibility; Natalie must obtain their confirmation before Jan 20 to validate the schedule change.

Karen Cho lacked system authority to mark the accommodation approved; the ADP entry is an unauthorized system change that should be reversed, and the accommodation request should be reprocessed through proper channels.

The interactive process was not completed (no essential functions analysis, no ER review, no documented dialogue with Okafor), AND the named respondent in an open investigation approved a term/condition of the complainant's employment — both the accommodation and investigation are now compromised.
The investigation case (CASE0013205) was never reassigned after Penner's departure, creating a procedural gap; the accommodation is valid but the investigation must be restarted from scratch.
